note: Single source of truth for /knowledge/saudi-e-invoicing-phase-2-checklist and for public/saudi-e-invoicing-phase-2-checklist.xlsx. The page imports this file; scripts/build-saudi-phase2-checklist.py reads the same file. Edit here, then re-run the script. Content is deliberately task-level rather than a restatement of ZATCA's technical specification, which is versioned and changes.

groups.title: Scope and channels
groups.blurb: Most of the cost of getting this wrong is decided here, before a single technical change is made.
items: Applicable wave confirmed from revenue subject to VAT in each of 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025, with the working retained rather than the conclusion alone.
Any notification received from ZATCA filed with the compliance record, and the assessment done without waiting for one to arrive.
Every channel that issues an invoice listed: ERP, each POS terminal, e-commerce platforms, billing and subscription systems, and any manual or spreadsheet invoicing still in use.
Each channel identified as issuing standard invoices, simplified invoices, or both, because the two follow different models.
Each channel confirmed as running a compliant e-invoicing solution, rather than producing a PDF and stopping there.
Integration deadline for the applicable wave recorded, and the plan worked backwards from it with the go-live date fixed first.

groups.title: Invoice data and structure
groups.blurb: The invoice the customer reads is not the invoice ZATCA receives. Both have to be right.
items: Structured invoice data generated in the required XML format, produced by the system rather than converted from a document.
Mandatory fields present and correctly populated for each invoice type, tested against real transactions and not only sample data.
A unique identifier generated for every invoice.
Hash chaining implemented so each invoice references the one before it, with the chain unbroken across restarts and channel outages.
QR code generated, and present on the invoice the customer actually receives where that is required.
Arabic present where required, and the invoice legible in the form it reaches the customer.

groups.title: Cryptography and connectivity
groups.blurb: This is where projects slip, because it is the part finance cannot complete without IT.
items: Cryptographic stamp identifier obtained and installed for every solution unit and device that issues invoices.
Onboarding completed for every POS terminal and every unit, not only the primary system.
Cryptographic stamping applied as required for the invoice type.
Connectivity to ZATCA tested from each channel through the firewall and network restrictions that will apply in production, not from a developer machine.
Credential expiry and renewal tracked with a named owner and a date, because a lapsed credential stops invoicing.

groups.title: Clearance and reporting
groups.blurb: Two flows, two sets of behaviour, including when ZATCA cannot be reached.
items: Standard invoices submitted for clearance before reaching the customer, with the cleared version being the one the customer receives.
Simplified invoices reported within the prescribed period after issuance.
Defined behaviour for a failed, delayed or rejected submission, agreed with the business before go-live rather than during an outage.
Credit and debit notes routed through the same flow as the invoice they relate to, carrying the reference and the reason.

groups.title: Process, controls and evidence
groups.blurb: Integration is the start of an ongoing control, not the end of a project.
items: Reconciliation between invoices issued in the source system and invoices accepted by ZATCA, run on a schedule with someone owning the differences.
Rejected and warned invoices monitored and cleared rather than allowed to accumulate.
Structured invoice data archived and retained, not only the human readable copy.
A named owner in finance and a named owner in IT, because this stops being deliverable the moment it is treated as a tax-only exercise.
End to end tests run in ZATCA's sandbox before go-live, covering every channel and every invoice type the business actually issues.
